name: Drop Cookie
description: Dough spooned or scooped directly onto a sheet pan, no rolling or shaping.

name: Rolled / Shaped Cookie
description: Dough rolled into balls or cut from a rolled sheet before baking.

name: Sandwich Cookie
description: Two baked pieces joined around a filling.

name: Bar / Shortbread
description: Pressed into a slab or block and cut after baking (or before).

name: Wafer / Iron-Cooked
description: Cooked in a hot iron rather than baked in an oven.

name: All-Purpose Flour
description: A moderate-protein flour giving balanced structure and chew.

name: Semolina
description: A coarser, higher-protein wheat product giving a distinct grainy short crumb.

name: Ground Nuts (in place of some flour)
description: Almonds or hazelnuts replacing part of the flour for a shorter, richer crumb.

name: Flour + Rice Flour / Cornstarch Blend
description: A small proportion of rice flour or cornstarch added for extra crumbliness or tenderness.

name: Butter
description: The most common cookie fat -- flavor and, depending on temperature, a major driver of spread.

name: Ghee / Clarified Butter
description: Butter with the milk solids removed -- a higher smoke point and a distinct nutty flavor, common where fresh butter historically didn't keep well.

name: Lard / Vegetable Shortening
description: A firmer, flavor-neutral (lard: distinctly savory) fat traditional to some shortbread-style cookies.

name: Minimal Added Fat (Egg-White Structure)
description: Almost no added butter or oil -- structure and richness instead come from ground almonds and whipped egg white.

name: Peanut Butter
description: Doubles as both fat and flavor -- rare among cookie fats for being a flavored ingredient in its own right.

name: Granulated Sugar
description: Promotes spread and crisp edges more than brown sugar does.

name: Brown Sugar
description: Its moisture content adds chew and a caramel depth granulated sugar doesn't have.

name: Powdered Sugar
description: Dissolves fully into a dough for an especially tender, short crumb, and is also the classic post-bake dusting.

name: Golden Syrup
description: A liquid sweetener that also acts as a binder in eggless doughs.

name: Dulce de Leche (as filling)
description: A cooked milk-and-sugar caramel used as the entire sweetening element of a filling, not mixed into the dough.

name: Baking Soda
description: The most common cookie leavener -- needs an acidic ingredient nearby to activate fully.

name: Cream of Tartar + Baking Soda
description: Cream of tartar supplies its own acidity, giving a distinctive soft tang alongside the lift.

name: Whipped Egg Whites
description: Mechanical, not chemical, leavening -- air whipped directly into the batter.

name: None (Unleavened)
description: A deliberate choice in short, crumbly traditions -- keeps the crumb dense rather than aerated.

name: Vanilla
description: The default American baking aromatic -- warm, sweet, and largely neutral against other flavors.

name: Cardamom
description: A warm, citrusy-floral spice central to South Asian baking identity.

name: Cinnamon
description: Both a coating (snickerdoodle) and an interior flavor note (Mexican polvorón) depending on tradition.

name: Orange Blossom / Rose Water
description: A floral aromatic central to Levantine pastry.

name: Salted Butter
description: A defining regional signature specifically in Breton baking, not a universal French trait.

name: Chocolate Chips / Chunks
description: Distinct pockets of chocolate folded through the dough rather than blended in.

name: Chopped Nuts
description: Adds crunch and a toasted flavor layer distinct from the base dough.

name: Rolled Oats + Desiccated Coconut
description: A structural mix-in that also acts as part of the recipe's binding, not just texture.

name: None
description: Many crumbly, filled, or wafer cookies deliberately have no mix-ins at all -- the point is a clean base dough.

name: None
description: The dough itself is the whole cookie -- no separate filling step.

name: Fruit Jam
description: Spread between two cookie layers, usually raspberry or apricot in the Linzer tradition.

name: Dulce de Leche
description: A thick caramel filling that's the entire point of the cookie, not an accent.

name: Date-Nut Paste
description: A sweetened date, walnut, or pistachio paste sealed inside a molded dough shell.

name: Caramel Syrup
description: A warm butter-and-syrup caramel sandwiched between two cooked wafer halves.

name: None (Plain)
description: No finishing step -- the baked surface is the finished cookie.

name: Powdered Sugar Dusting
description: Applied strictly after baking, for both sweetness and visual finish.

name: Cinnamon-Sugar Coating
description: Applied before baking, so it becomes part of the crust rather than sitting on top of it.

name: Chocolate Coating
description: A full or partial dip, common as a documented regional variation rather than the base recipe.
